Paragraph:
Translation: One who restrains his senses and fixes his consciousness upon Me is known as a man of steady intelligence.

Purport (Excerpt): ...unless one is Krsna conscious, it is not at all possible to control the senses... King Ambarisa fixed his mind on the lotus feet of Lord Krsna, engaged his words in describing the abode of the Lord, his hands in cleansing the temple... and all these qualifications made him fit to become a mat-parah devotee... The senses can be completely controlled only by the strength of devotional service to Krsna.
Situation/Problem_Faced: The realization that willpower alone is insufficient to control impetuous sensory cravings leads to the problem of finding a reliable method for mastering the mind.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna introduces the ultimate solution for sensory control: redirecting and occupying every single sense in the active service of the Divine (Mat-parah) rather than artificially suppressing them.
Outcome/Resolution: By anchoring consciousness in the Supreme, the mind naturally attains steady intelligence without the friction of constant internal warfare.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Channeling Energy vs. Suppression: Actively employing senses in meaningful tasks instead of trying to silence them
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Behavioral Engagement: Using physical and mental actions to support internal focus
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Anchoring Attention: Fixing consciousness on a transcendent point of focus (Mat-parah)

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Mat-parah (Taking the Supreme as the ultimate goal/shelter)
Yukta-vairagya (Utilizing sense organs actively in sacred service)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Sensory control is impossible through mere negation. True mastery is achieved when all physical and mental faculties—eyes, ears, hands, words—are fully occupied in devotional service to Krishna. As illustrated by King Ambarisa, engaging the senses in divine work naturally neutralizes material desires.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This verse presents a foundational behavioral strategy: replacement over suppression. When we try to force the mind *not* to think about a craving, it fixates on it further. By actively engaging the body and mind in high-purpose, values-driven activities, we redirect our psychological bandwidth, allowing self-control to occur effortlessly.
